question.text: The linear form $f(\mathbf{x})$ is defined as $f(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{a} \mathbf{x},$ where $\mathbf{a}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -3 \end{bmatrix}.$ Evaluate the function when $\mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ \, \, 2 \end{bmatrix}.$
question.explanation:
Substituting $\mathbf{x} = \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ \, \, 2 \end{bmatrix},$ we obtain

\begin{align*} f(\mathbf{x}) &= \mathbf{a} \mathbf{x} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -3\end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ \, \, 2 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= 1 \cdot (-1) + (-3) \cdot 2 \\[5pt] &= -1 - 6 \\[5pt] &= -7. \end{align*}

question.text:
Consider the bilinear form $B(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}),$ given by

\[ B(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})= 2x_1y_1-x_2y_1 + 3x_1y_2 -x_2y_2 . \]

Evaluate $B(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})$ when $\mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{y}=\begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}.$
question.explanation:
We are given that

$\qquad$ $\mathbf{x} = \begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}\quad$ and $\quad \mathbf{y} = \begin{bmatrix} y_1 \\ y_2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}.$

Substituting these into the bilinear expression, we obtain

\begin{align*} B(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}) &= 2x_1y_1-x_2y_1 + 3x_1y_2 -x_2y_2 \\[3pt] &= 2\cdot (-1)\cdot(-2) - 2\cdot (-2) +3\cdot (-1)\cdot 1-2\cdot 1 \\[3pt] &= 4 +4 -3 -2 \\[3pt] &= 3. \end{align*}

Evaluate $B(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})$ when $\mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\\end{bmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{y}=\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}.$
question.explanation:
We are given that

$\qquad$ $\mathbf{x} = \begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}\quad$ and $\quad \mathbf{y} = \begin{bmatrix} y_1 \\ y_2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}.$

Substituting these into the bilinear expression, we obtain

\begin{align*} B(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}) &= x_1y_1+x_2y_1 + 2x_1y_2 +x_2y_2 \\[3pt] &= 1\cdot 3 + 1\cdot 3 +2\cdot 1\cdot (-1)+1\cdot (-1) \\[3pt] &= 3 + 3 -2 - 1 \\[3pt] &= 3. \end{align*}

Evaluate $B(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})$ when $\mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 2 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{y}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}.$
question.explanation:
We are given that

$\qquad$ $\mathbf{x} = \begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \\ x_3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 2 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}\quad$ and $\quad \mathbf{y} = \begin{bmatrix} y_1 \\ y_2 \\ y_3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}.$

Substituting these into the bilinear expression, we obtain

\begin{align*} B(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}) &= 2x_1y_2 - 4x_2y_3 + x_3y_1 -3 x_3y_2 \\[3pt] &= 2\cdot (-2) \cdot 0 - 4 \cdot 2 \cdot 3 + (-1) \cdot 1 - 3 \cdot (-1)\cdot 0 \\[3pt] &= 0 - 24 -1 - 0 \\[3pt] &= -25. \end{align*}

question.text: \[ A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \] Consider the matrix $A$ above. Which of the following represents the corresponding bilinear form $\mathbf{x}^T \! A \mathbf{y}$ in terms of the components of $\mathbf{x} = \begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{y} = \begin{bmatrix} y_1 \\ y_2 \end{bmatrix}?$
question.explanation:
Method 1

Each entry $a_{ij}$ of $A$ corresponds to the term $a_{ij}x_i y_j$ in the expression of the bilinear form:

\begin{align*} \mathbf{x}^T \! A \mathbf{y} &= \bbox[2pt,lightgray]{2}x_1y_1 + \bbox[2pt,lightgray]{3}x_1y_2 + \bbox[2pt,lightgray]{1}x_2y_1 + \bbox[2pt,lightgray]{2}x_2y_2 \\[3pt] &= 2x_1y_1 + 3x_1y_2 + x_2y_1 + 2x_2y_2 \end{align*}

Method 2

To write down a bilinear form in terms of vector components, we compute the following expression:

\begin{align*} \mathbf{x}^T \! A \mathbf{y} &= \begin{bmatrix} x_1 & x_2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} y_1 \\ y_2 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} x_1 & x_2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 2y_1+3y_2 \\ y_1+2y_2 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= x_1(2y_1+3y_2) + x_2(y_1+2y_2) \\[5pt] &= 2x_1y_1 + 3x_1y_2 + x_2y_1 +2 x_2y_2 \end{align*}

question.text: \[ \begin{bmatrix} \bbox[2pt,lightgray]{a} & \!\!-2 \\[2pt] 0 & \bbox[2pt,lightgray]{b} \end{bmatrix} \] The matrix of the bilinear form $B(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}) = x_1y_1-2x_1y_2 + 2x_2y_2$ is given above. What is the value of $a+b?$
question.explanation:
Each term $a_{ij}x_i y_j$ in the expression of the bilinear form corresponds to the entry $a_{ij}$ of the matrix:

\begin{align*} B(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}) &= x_1y_1-2x_1y_2 + 2x_2y_2 \\[3pt] &= {\color{blue}1}x_1y_1+({\color{blue}-2})x_1y_2\\[3pt] &+\hspace{0.2mm} {\color{blue}0}x_2y_1 \, + {\color{blue}2}x_2y_2 \end{align*}

Then, the corresponding matrix of the bilinear form is

\[ \begin{bmatrix} \bbox[2pt,lightgray]{1} & \!\!-2 \\[2pt] 0 & \bbox[2pt,lightgray]{2} \end{bmatrix}. \]

Therefore, $a=1$ and $b=2.$ Finally, \[ a+b=1+2 = 3. \]

What is the value of $a+b+c?$
question.explanation:
Each term $a_{ij}x_i y_j$ in the expression of the bilinear form corresponds to the entry $a_{ij}$ of the matrix:

\begin{align*} B(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}) &= x_1y_2+ 3x_2y_1 - 3x_3 y_2+2x_3y_3 \\[3pt] &= {\color{blue}0}x_1y_1+{\color{blue}1}x_1y_2+{\color{blue}0}x_1y_3 \\[3pt] &+\hspace{0.5mm} {\color{blue}3}x_2y_1 + {\color{blue}0}x_2y_2 + {\color{blue}0}x_2y_3 \\[3pt] &+\hspace{0.5mm} {\color{blue}0}x_3y_1 + ({\color{blue}-3})x_3y_2 + {\color{blue}2}x_3 y_3 \end{align*}

Then, the corresponding matrix of the bilinear form is

\[ \begin{bmatrix} 0 & \bbox[2pt,lightgray]{1} & 0 \\[3pt] \bbox[2pt,lightgray]{3} & 0 & 0 \\[3pt] 0 & -3 & \bbox[2pt,lightgray]{2} \end{bmatrix}. \]

Therefore, $a=1,$ $b=3,$ and $c=2.$ Finally, \[ a+b+c=1+3+2 = 6. \]
